summary: A re-release of RFC 1067 with a changed status section. It defines a simple protocol for inspecting or altering management information on a network element from a remote location. It was replaced by RFC 1157.

eli5.summary: Network devices have settings and counters. This is a simple way to ask a device what is going on, or to tell it to change a setting, from far away.

questions: simple network management protocol original spec
subtitle: A simple protocol for remote inspection and control of network device management information.

tldr.problem: Network operators need to monitor and control devices like routers and hosts from a central management station, but existing network management protocols are complex.
tldr.mechanism: SNMP uses a simple request-response model where a management station sends get, set, or query messages to agents on network devices, which respond with the requested information or status changes.
tldr.outcome: Networks can be managed efficiently from central locations without complex management logic on every device. SNMP became a foundational protocol for network management. This was replaced by RFC 1157.

today: RFC 1098 was replaced by RFC 1157. SNMP became a foundational standard for network management and is still widely deployed in networks today, though newer versions (SNMPv2, SNMPv3) with improved security have been developed.

sections.title: Network Management Basics
sections.content:
Network management requires monitoring and controlling network elements such as hosts, routers, and terminal servers. SNMP enables this by allowing a management station to communicate with management agents running on network devices. The protocol uses an unreliable datagram service (UDP) and places minimal complexity on the agents themselves, keeping management agent software simple and inexpensive to develop.

The design philosophy minimizes the number of essential management functions on agents to just two: retrieve a value (get) and alter a value (set). Monitoring is accomplished primarily through polling from the management center, with a limited number of unsolicited trap messages to alert the center to important events. This approach avoids the complexity of imperative commands and keeps network traffic low.
sections.eli5: Network devices have a simple helper (agent) that answers questions and follows simple instructions from a central manager instead of a complex system on each device.

sections.title: The SNMP Architecture
sections.content:
SNMP defines three key concepts: management stations that execute management applications, network elements (devices) that contain agents, and the SNMP protocol that communicates between them. The protocol represents management information using a subset of ASN.1 (Abstract Syntax Notation One), the same language used in SGMP (the earlier Simple Gateway Monitoring Protocol).

Management information is organized in a tree structure called the Management Information Base (MIB). Each managed object in the MIB has a unique name (an Object Identifier or OID) and can be accessed only through allowed operations. The protocol is independent of the architecture of particular hosts or gateways, making it broadly applicable across diverse network equipment.
sections.eli5: A management station is like a control room, agents on devices are helpers in each building, and SNMP is the language they use to talk to each other about device settings and counters.

sections.title: Protocol Data Units and Messages
sections.content:
SNMP communicates through five types of protocol data units (PDUs): GetRequest (ask for a value), GetNextRequest (retrieve the next value in the MIB tree, used for table traversal), GetResponse (the response to a get or set), SetRequest (alter a value), and Trap (an unsolicited alert). All messages travel in UDP datagrams on port 161 for requests and responses, port 162 for traps.

Each message includes a version number, a community name (which defines an SNMP community and access policy), and a PDU. The community name acts as a simple form of authentication: all messages from application entities in the same community share a community name, and an SNMP agent uses the community name to select an access profile that determines which management information is readable or writable.
sections.eli5: SNMP messages are like mail: some ask for information, some change settings, some are just notifications of problems. Each message says who is sending it (the community) so the receiver knows what information to share.

sections.title: Get, Set, and Trap Operations
sections.content:
A GetRequest contains one or more variable names and returns their values in a GetResponse. If any requested variable does not exist or cannot be retrieved, an error status is returned. A SetRequest changes the values of one or more variables, and the agent responds with a GetResponse indicating success or an error. The SetRequest is atomic: either all assignments succeed or all fail together.

Trap messages are generated by agents to report significant events without waiting for a management station to poll. Standard trap types include coldStart (agent restarting), warmStart (agent reinitializing without configuration change), linkDown/linkUp (interface status), authenticationFailure (bad community name), egpNeighborLoss (EGP routing neighbor lost), and enterpriseSpecific (vendor-defined events). Traps guide the timing and focus of polling, reducing the need for constant polling of all devices.
sections.eli5: The manager asks questions (get), gives orders (set), and devices send urgent messages when something important happens (trap) instead of waiting to be asked.

sections.title: Management Information and Communities
sections.content:
Management information is represented as instances of managed objects defined in the MIB. An SNMP MIB view is a subset of MIB objects that pertain to a particular network element. An SNMP community is a pairing of an agent with a set of SNMP application entities, each identified by a community name. An SNMP access policy defines the access privileges (read-only or read-write) to a specific MIB view for a specific community.

Proxy agents can monitor and control devices that do not directly support SNMP by translating between SNMP and other protocols. This allows a management station to apply a consistent management framework across diverse equipment, including legacy devices like modems and multiplexors. Proxy agents also shield network elements from complex access control policies by implementing sophisticated access control at the proxy layer.
sections.eli5: Communities are groups of allowed managers and devices that trust each other. An agent keeps track of what information each community can see or change, and a proxy agent translates SNMP to older systems.
